newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia probe criticises aviation authority.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia probe criticises aviation authority.

text.p: Australia's former Civil Aviation Authority was strongly criticised by a crash inquiry on Tuesday, including an accusation that it was too timid in dealing with the industry.
The inquiry into Australia's 1994 Seaview air crash, in which nine people died, found that the plane was overloaded and the pilot held an invalid licence.
"The aircraft was seriously overloaded and the documentation associated with the flight sought to disguise the overload," the report said.

The report into relations between the Civil Aviation Authority and Seaview Air found Seaview was an unsafe organisation which breached regulations and the authority had failed to act as a safety watchdog.
Seaview's Rockwell Aero Commander crashed into the sea en route from Newcastle to Lord Howe Island on October 2, 1994.
The aircraft was overloaded by between 261 and 288 kg, Transport Minister John Sharp said in a statement accompanying the report.
"The report found Seaview pilots regularly overloaded aircraft primarily due to the subtle but unmistakable pressure exerted by Seaview's management," Sharp said.
The report said the authority had also placed commercial interests above passenger safety.
"In its efforts to please and appease industry, the management of the authority seemed to regard standards set by the regulations and orders as negotiable," Sharp said.
The report recommended that papers be referred to the Director of Public Prosecutions to consider possible prosecutions.
The goverment will prepare a response to the report by the end of the year.
The authority has since been reorganised as Civil Aviation Safety Authority.
